local_entities.label: Voyager as experienced within malfunctioning simulation

evidence.summary: The Doctor experiences an apparently abandoned/damaged Voyager, remote projection, injury, and events that later prove to be generated inside a malfunctioning holodeck/program feedback state.
Computer records and a Barclay figure present the Doctor as human Lewis Zimmerman and Voyager as his simulation.
evidence.counterevidence: Later within the same unstable frame, this explanation is contradicted.

evidence.summary: The Doctor tests competing explanations by replaying apparent memories and destroying a simulated holographic memory core without collapsing the perceived ship.
A Chakotay projection says the Doctor himself is trapped in a holodeck feedback loop and will be destroyed if he terminates the simulated Voyager; Barclay gives the opposite warning.
The Doctor is restored to the holodeck/ship context, identifies himself again as Voyager's EMH, and reflects on why the malfunction centered on whether he is a person or projection.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: A radiation-induced feedback event traps the Doctor in nested and contradictory reality explanations.
neutral_coding.epistemics: All pre-recovery events are scoped as unreliable simulation/delusion rather than promoted to ship history.
neutral_coding.identity_self_concept: The episode explicitly stages person-versus-projection questions without requiring a metaphysical ruling.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Even the apparent recovery is followed by residual questioning, though the source then returns to ordinary Voyager context.
